assumptions: The existing Linux host can run two containers and host a small import script.
VPN access is the primary access control boundary.
Daily host backups satisfy the 24-hour RPO and 1-day RTO.
The CSV format is stable enough for a simple monthly import script.

components.name: FastAPI Directory Service
components.purpose: Serve read-only HTML staff directory pages to VPN-only employees.

components.name: PostgreSQL Directory Database
components.purpose: Store 100 read-only staff names and work phone numbers, with monthly CSV import support.

components.name: Monthly CSV Import Script
components.purpose: Import or upsert the monthly staff CSV into PostgreSQL without adding another container.

implementation_steps: Create a PostgreSQL container with a staff directory database and a small staff table.
Create a FastAPI container that reads the staff table and renders read-only HTML pages.
Restrict both containers to the internal Linux host and VPN-only access.
Write a psql/SQL import script that performs an idempotent monthly CSV upsert.
Document the monthly import procedure and verify daily host backups.
architecture.summary: A minimal two-container internal directory on the existing Linux host, with FastAPI serving read-only HTML pages and PostgreSQL storing 100 staff records. Monthly CSV import is handled by a simple host-side psql/SQL script, preserving zero incremental hosting cost and low maintenance.
architecture.title: Cost-Effective Internal Staff Directory
tradeoffs: A host-side import script is cheaper and simpler than adding an automation platform.
Manual or scheduled import execution is acceptable because the workload is small and monthly.
Business-hours availability is met without high-availability infrastructure.

required_changes: Bind both containers to the internal/VPN interface only and disable public port exposure.
Create a read-only PostgreSQL role for FastAPI and a separate import role for CSV upserts.
Make the monthly CSV import transactional, idempotent, validated, and logged, with a documented rollback procedure.
Include the PostgreSQL data volume in daily host backups and perform a restore test to confirm the 1-day RTO.
risks: Misconfigured container networking could expose the directory or database to non-VPN networks.
Manual CSV import may introduce bad data if validation, idempotency, or rollback are not enforced.
Daily host backups may not include the PostgreSQL data volume or may not have been tested for restore.
Lack of monitoring could delay detection of a downed directory during business hours.

avoid_list: Any public-facing import UI or integration platform

candidates.cost_profile: Zero incremental hosting cost on the existing Linux host; low maintenance if kept as a single container with daily backups.
candidates.name: PostgreSQL
candidates.performance_profile: More than sufficient for 100 read-only records and one-second response during business hours.
candidates.rationale: PostgreSQL is the simplest established option and satisfies the hard constraints. The evidence is sufficient to support basic CSV import and idempotent upsert, though it is not a performance benchmark.
candidates.role: Primary relational store for names and work phone numbers, with monthly CSV import and read-only FastAPI access.
candidates.scalability: Adequate for current scale and can grow far beyond 100 records without architectural change.
strengths: Already part of the existing stack.
Supplied evidence supports PostgreSQL CSV import and idempotent upsert patterns.
Small relational dataset fits PostgreSQL well.
Read-only access and daily host backups align with the stated RPO/RTO.
weaknesses: Requires container management and backup discipline.
Supplied snippets do not provide latency benchmarks or FastAPI integration details.

candidates.cost_profile: No additional software cost; minimal developer time for a small script or SQL file.
candidates.name: psql / SQL import script
candidates.performance_profile: Instant for 100 records; no meaningful impact on one-second response target.
candidates.rationale: This is the preferred import approach because it is simple, low-cost, and aligned with the two-container constraint. Evidence is sufficient for the core pattern but weak on operational details.
candidates.role: Monthly CSV import mechanism using PostgreSQL's CSV import and idempotent upsert logic.
candidates.scalability: Sufficient for monthly imports of a small table; can be extended if record count grows.
strengths: Avoids adding another container or service.
Idempotent upsert is supported by supplied evidence.
Simplest path for a one-week build.
weaknesses: Manual or scheduled execution must be documented.
No evidence in supplied snippets about error handling, logging, or rollback.

candidates.cost_profile: Potentially zero incremental hosting cost if self-hosted, but adds operational overhead and possible licensing considerations not covered by supplied evidence.
candidates.name: n8n
candidates.performance_profile: Likely sufficient for 100 records, but no supplied evidence quantifies latency or reliability.
candidates.rationale: n8n is not justified by the supplied evidence for this use case. It may be useful for larger pipelines, but it adds complexity without a clear benefit for five users and 100 records.
candidates.role: Emerging workflow option for monthly CSV import into PostgreSQL.
candidates.scalability: Can scale beyond this use case, but that is unnecessary for 100 records and monthly imports.
strengths: Supplied evidence mentions n8n for ETL and idempotent Postgres loads.
Could centralize import logic if the process grows.
weaknesses: Adds another service or container to manage.
No supplied evidence on cost, security, backup, or operational complexity.
Novelty does not create a material benefit for this small, monthly, read-only workload.

candidates.cost_profile: No incremental hosting cost if used only for initial seeding, but no evidence of licensing or operational cost.
candidates.name: Seedfast
candidates.performance_profile: Not relevant to monthly import or runtime response; no supplied evidence on performance.
candidates.rationale: Seedfast is insufficient evidence for this requirement and is not a material improvement over plain SQL or psql import.
candidates.role: Alternative seeding approach for initial database population.
candidates.scalability: Not needed for current scale; evidence suggests plain SQL is simpler for small reference data.
strengths: Supplied evidence mentions seeding PostgreSQL databases.
weaknesses: Evidence is weak and does not address monthly CSV import, idempotency, or the two-container constraint.
Adds an unnecessary tool for a 100-record directory.

evaluation.industry_baseline: For a five-user, 100-record internal directory, the baseline is a minimal FastAPI + PostgreSQL deployment on an existing Linux host, with monthly CSV imports handled by simple SQL/psql operations rather than a full ETL platform.
key_tradeoffs: Simplicity versus automation: plain psql/SQL import is simpler and cheaper, while n8n adds workflow automation but also operational complexity.
Established tooling versus emerging tooling: PostgreSQL and psql are well-supported by the supplied evidence; n8n and Seedfast are less justified for this small workload.
Two-container constraint versus added services: adding n8n or another import platform may violate the simplicity and cost goals unless it replaces an existing service.

request.problem: Build a tiny internal read-only staff directory for five employees on our existing VPN. FastAPI serves HTML and PostgreSQL stores 100 names and work phone numbers. An admin imports CSV monthly. No public access, login UI, integrations, attachments or regulated data. Deploy two containers on our existing Linux host; our VPN and daily host backups handle access control and recovery. Budget: zero incremental hosting cost. One developer, one week. Business-hours availability, one-second latency, 24-hour RPO and one-day RTO. Assume remaining details; no clarification is needed. Keep the design to two or three components, compare three relevant technologies, and use three focused research queries on official FastAPI and PostgreSQL documentation.
